parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.stem:
Copper can form complexes with the ligands ammonia and $en$, $\text{H}_2\text{NCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$, as shown.

$$[\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}(\text{aq}) + en(\text{aq}) \rightleftharpoons [\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4(en)]^{2+}(\text{aq}) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l}) \quad K_{\text{stab}} = 3.98 \times 10^{10} \text{ equilibrium 4}$$

$$[\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}(\text{aq}) + 2\text{NH}_3(\text{aq}) \rightleftharpoons [\text{Cu}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4(\text{NH}_3)_2]^{2+}(\text{aq}) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l}) \quad K_{\text{stab}} = 5.01 \times 10^{7} \text{ equilibrium 5}$$
parts.text:

parts.text:
The standard entropy change, $\Delta S^\ominus$, for equilibrium 4 is $+23\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$ and for equilibrium 5 is $-8.4\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$.

parts.text: Of the three copper complexes in equilibria 4 and 5, state the formula of the copper complex that is the most stable and explain your choice.
